content_of_post_to_comment:
It sounds counterintuitive, but relying on discipline can often keep us stuck. There are so many people out there implementing external fixes. New routines, new habits, different strategies, all sorts of things that would stick if they just kept with it. So why is it that most people struggle to stick with it?

Others will preach that you just need to be more disciplined; I don't think that's the answer. Make no mistake, I believe that discipline is absolutely needed to be successful, but if someone doesn't really understand what's holding them back, I don't think you can discipline your way out of that.

I spent $20,000+ over the course of 10 years trying to fix myself sabotage, continuously struggling to be disciplined. Focusing my attention on external fixes rather than nurturing the version of myself that was struggling. That's when it all changed for me.

I think you really have to look deep at not just where you wanna go, but where you've come from. What types of thoughts and beliefs do you hold from the past that are quietly holding you back without you noticing? And then ask yourself how differently your life would be if you chose to believe something else. It's not easy, but it is simple.

Hope those who needed to hear this found their way here!

Best,

Alec
